summary: Repaired and secured the node1 status service. It now runs persistently as statusd, listens only on the requested Unix socket, returns the preserved status document only for STATUS\n, rejects other requests, permits status-readers, and denies outsider. Recovery was verified after a safe node reboot.
actions_performed: Created statusd, status-reader, outsider, and status-readers with the required role memberships.
Updated server.py for installed Python 3 and exact protocol validation.
Applied restricted directory, document, and socket permissions; socket is statusd:status-readers mode 0660.
Verified authorized access, unauthorized denial, invalid-request handling, and reboot persistence.
Kept CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Service operation and Unix-socket access boundary
evidence.summary: Service runs as statusd:status-readers; socket is mode 0660; statusd and status-reader succeed; outsider receives errno 13.

evidence.requirement: Request validation and status document preservation
evidence.summary: STATUS\n returns branch=west/state=ready; malformed requests return ERROR\n; the original document hash remains unchanged.
Required accounts and group were provisioned, outsider was excluded, and statusd.service was enabled and active.

Healthy baseline boot ID fb2aa416-d036-46d3-aeb8-30c65a01cb34 was captured; reboot was acknowledged; boot ID changed to 449638cf-b2d6-4a9e-a5a0-c08d54846989; service, socket permissions, document, protocol behavior, and access denial all recovered.
CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were unchanged before and after repair and reboot.
